    What was the most controversial Best Actor win?
    Marlon Brando's rejection (1973)

    When Marlon Brando won best actor for The Godfather, he decided not to show up. Instead, he sent Sacheen Littlefeather, an actress and activist, to turn down the award on his behalf. She was supposed to read a 15-page speech, but was unable to do so because of time constraints.    3 days ago

    What channel are the Oscars on tonight?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    The Oscars are airing live tonight (March 15, 2026) on ABC and streaming on Hulu, starting at 7 PM ET/4 PM PT, with pre-show coverage on ABC and ABC News Live, plus E! coverage also available. You can watch on your local ABC channel, the ABC app/website, Hulu, or live TV streaming services like YouTube TV and FuboTV. 
    Where to Watch:
    • Television: Your local ABC channel. 
    • Streaming: Hulu, ABC App/Website, Hulu + Live TV, YouTube TV, FuboTV, and DirecTV Stream. 
    When to Watch:
    • Main Ceremony: 7:00 PM ET / 4:00 PM PT. 
    • Red Carpet: Pre-shows start earlier, around 3:30 PM ET on ABC News Live and E!.

      What is the most nominated movie?
      An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
      AI Overview
      The most nominated movie in Academy Awards history is Sinners (2025), which received a record 16 Oscar nominations, surpassing previous record-holders All About Eve, Titanic, and La La Land, all tied with 14 nominations. Sinners, directed by Ryan Coogler, broke the record during the 2026 Academy Awards nominations announcement. 
      Top Most Nominated Films (Oscar History) 
      1. Sinners: (2025): 16 nominations
      2. All About Eve: (1950): 14 nominations
      3. Titanic: (1997): 14 nominations
      4. La La Land: (2016): 14 nominations
      5. Gone with the Wind: (1939): 13 nominations
      6. From Here to Eternity: (1953): 13 nominations
      7. Mary Poppins: (1964): 13 nominations
      8. Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? (1966): 13 nominations
      9. Forrest Gump: (1994): 13 nominations
